system_components.ingestion: Upload endpoints, format routing (PDF/DOCX/PPTX/CSV/XLSX), redaction, chunking (500-1000 tokens with overlap), and processing state tracking.

system_components.evaluation: Synthetic corpus generation + presidio-research metrics, sprint efficacy script (B1.6).
system_components.rag_pipeline: Planned for Sprint 02: query embedding, vector search, GPT-4o-mini generation, context compression, semantic caching, tiered routing.

HYG-2 learning — a deferral's stated blocker is a claim, not a fact; run it before inheriting it. Next-step #368 sat undone because Sprint 55 recorded that guarding the alembic email derivation "would fail `alembic upgrade head` for any operator with a bare AUTH_USERNAME". Tested against real PostgreSQL 15, that is false: Alembic does not re-run an applied revision, and migration 023 additionally returns early when the users table exists, so a database already past 023 upgrades cleanly with AUTH_USERNAME=kneelinghorse. The guard cost one function and four tests; the deferral cost a sprint. When a next-step explains why something was NOT done, treat that explanation as the first thing to verify — especially when the work looks small and the reason sounds structural. Proof: cmos/reports/sprint-56/hyg-2-migration-guard-proof.py.

HYG-2 learning — a skip marker's stated reason rots silently, and a stale one hides a passing test. tests/integration/test_rag_pipeline.py skipped TWO tests for "openai/httpx version incompatibility — httpx removed 'proxies' kwarg; needs openai SDK upgrade". Installed openai is 2.24.0 and passes no such kwarg, so the reason was stale: un-skipped, test_rag_pipeline_returns_cached_payload PASSES and had been suppressed for a reason never true of it, while its sibling test_rag_pipeline_generates_cited_answer fails on an unrelated undiagnosed change (_StubRetrievalService.calls empty at line 177 — the pipeline never reaches the stub). Two rules: (1) a skip reason naming a dependency must be re-tested whenever that dependency moves, or it becomes a permanent exemption nobody re-reads; (2) when investigating a reported error, grep the repo for the error's own text before trusting the reporter's attribution — next-step #369 called this an httpx/starlette venv skew, and grepping the string "proxies" led straight to the real source, the openai SDK. Same family as the Sprint 55 decision that a check which cannot fail is not evidence: a test that can never run is not coverage.

HYG-2 learning — lint every changed FILE, not every changed source file. CI's ruff-diff lints the full changed-file set, receipts and archived proof scripts under cmos/reports/ included, and it installs a PINNED ruff (0.8.0 per .github/workflows/backend-lint.yml) that can differ from the local one. PR #338's only red was S603 in an archived proof script that had never been linted locally, because the local pass covered only app/tests/alembic sources. Before pushing, run: ruff check $(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | grep '\.py$') with ruff==0.8.0 installed. Related trap already recorded: a pre-existing lint error in a file you touch becomes YOUR CI failure, because ruff-diff scopes to changed files — migration 023 carried an untouched I001 that only surfaced once this mission edited the file.

RBAC-5 learning — a positive control can pass for the wrong reason, and only a mutation test will say so. The first implementation of the project-owner read positive (next-step #367) seeded the fixture document AS THE MEMBER. That makes document.owner_id == the member, so authorize() returns True at the plain owner clause (app/core/authorization.py:143) and the project-owner path below it — the actual clause under test — never executes. The check was green, the run reported a closed vacuous row, and the claim was false. It was caught only by injecting a mutant that disabled the project-owner clause outright and finding the check STILL green. Seeding the document as the OWNER produces the only shape that reaches the clause: a document the member does not own, inside a project the member does. Rule: for any positive control, ask which branch of the policy it proves, then mutate that exact branch and require red. "The test passes" and "the test tests the thing" are different claims, and deny-only matrices are especially prone to this — a matrix with no positive control passes just as happily on a system that denies everyone.

RBAC-5 learning — two test files cover scripts/rbac_verify.py, not one, and running only the obvious one shipped a red CI. tests/test_rbac_verify_harness.py (2040 lines) is the one everything points at; tests/test_rbac_verify_mutation_proof.py (100 lines) also imports from the harness module and is where the RBAC-3 fail-open mutation proof lives. Removing _THROWAWAY_PASSWORD broke the second file with an ImportError that no local run caught, because every local run was scoped to the first file by explicit path. That path-scoping habit comes from a real constraint (learning: run migration tests by explicit file path, because -k collection breaks on two files), but it cuts the other way when a change removes a module-level symbol. Two cheap rules: after deleting or renaming any module-level name, grep the whole tree for it before pushing; and for a change to a widely imported module, run CI's own invocation locally — `pytest --ignore=tests/integration` with the 12 quarantine deselects from .github/ci/backend-quarantine.txt — rather than a hand-picked file list.

PERF-1 reconnaissance (read-only; the mission is still Queued and untouched). The Sprint 52 aggregates decision #426 deferred budgets for are reachable as: GET /graph/neighborhood and GET /graph/stats, both in app/api/v1/graph_neighborhood.py (lines 24 and 46); the attention dashboards (saved exception views, UX-12); and the priority inbox (UX-13). Material finding for whoever picks this up: THERE IS NO SERVER-TIMING INFRASTRUCTURE AT ALL — a grep across app/ for Server-Timing, X-Response-Time and process_time returns nothing. So decision #458's two permitted forms are not equally cheap here. The "server timing" form needs new middleware or per-route instrumentation before any budget can be expressed; the "feature p95 minus a trivial-endpoint p95 measured from the same client in the same run" form needs only a committed measurement script and is the smaller path to a first budget. Recommend the baseline-relative form first, with a trivial endpoint such as /api/v1/health as the subtrahend, and treat server timings as a separate decision rather than folding them in silently. Whichever form is chosen, decision #458 also requires the receipt to record the baseline NEXT TO the feature measurement, and the mission's own criterion requires that an exceeded budget fail something — if it lands advisory-only, the receipt must say so in those words rather than implying enforcement.

PERF-1 recon, part 2 — there is already a home and a harness, so PERF-1 should extend rather than invent. tests/performance/ exists and pytest-benchmark is installed and running in CI (the backend suite prints a 'rag_concurrency' benchmark table). But note what the one existing benchmark actually asserts: tests/performance/test_concurrent_queries.py::test_concurrent_queries_reaches_target_throughput ends with `assert service.count >= 100` — a COUNT, not a time. It measures a synthetic in-process stub with a time.sleep(0.0005), so it is a throughput smoke, not a budget, and nothing in it would fail if an endpoint got ten times slower. Combined with part 1 (no Server-Timing/process_time infrastructure anywhere in app/) and the absolute-millisecond assertions in tests/test_semantic_edge_e2e_validation.py, the picture is: TraceLab has performance TESTS but no performance BUDGET in decision #458's sense, and the two things that look like budgets are the two shapes #458 forbids. Suggested shape for PERF-1: put it in tests/performance/ on pytest-benchmark, drive the real app against real PostgreSQL via testcontainers (production measurement is blocked on the same credential as the RBAC matrix), and express every assertion as feature-p95 minus a trivial-endpoint p95 measured in the same run.

(1) The Stage1 MCP server runs with cwd '/' and fails with `ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir '/out'` on any call that writes artifacts, unless an explicit writable `outDir` is passed. That is the first thing to set; it is NOT the "Connection closed" aggregator symptom recorded in memory, and it does not mean the server is unhealthy — with outDir set, inspect_app completed 21 passes with zero failed or degraded. (2) stage1_list_runs also searches the server's cwd (/out/stage1) and therefore reports "No Stage1 runs found" even when runs exist, so it cannot be used to locate the baseline; find the baseline on disk instead. (3) THE APRIL BASELINE IS IN THE TRACELAB REPO ITSELF, not in any Stage1 tree: out/stage1/tracelab-prod-guided/guided-1776917221458/ (17 authenticated routes, complete artifact set) and out/stage1/tracelab-prod/5200dec3-00d2-4c9f-b5eb-abd4e0777715/ (the 8-route unauthenticated pass). BOTH ARE UNDER out/, WHICH IS GITIGNORED — they exist on this machine only, and losing this machine loses the only fingerprint baseline the project has. Copying guided-1776917221458 somewhere tracked should happen before the next scan, independently of whether the scan runs. (4) compareRunDir requires infer:true and produces drift_report.json; the comparison is against orca_candidates, so a like-for-like route set matters more than the artifact names suggest — comparing an unauthenticated run to the authenticated baseline would produce dozens of spurious "disappeared" entries with no real meaning.

THE SPRINT 55 GITIGNORE DEFECT RECURRED, in a new form, and was caught only by reading `git status` rather than trusting the copy. Sprint 55 found cmos/.gitignore's blanket `*.log` hiding all 21 evidence logs under cmos/reports across three sprints — every receipt citing one was citing a file that existed on a single machine. This session hit the identical class with a different pattern: `.gitignore:61 artifacts/` (a rule for local packaging output) silently swallowed all 18 files of the preserved Stage1 fingerprint baseline; only manifest.json staged. The receipt already said the baseline was preserved. Without checking the staged file count, the commit would have shipped a receipt citing 18 files that were never committed — the exact failure Sprint 55 spent a mission cleaning up. Fixed with a targeted negation (!cmos/reports/baselines/**/artifacts/ plus /**) rather than by weakening the packaging rule, with a comment at both rules. THE DURABLE RULE: after copying evidence into a tracked path, `git add` it and then COUNT what actually staged against what you copied. `git check-ignore -v <one representative file>` answers it in one call. Blanket ignore rules written for build output (*.log, artifacts/, dist/, out/) are the recurring hazard, because evidence directories naturally use the same names. Related and still true: the project's only design fingerprint baseline lived solely under the gitignored out/ until this session, so it would have died with the laptop.
